section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a single study validating the Portuguese version of the Acceptance of Cosmetic Surgery Scale (ACSS) using exploratory factor analysis and reliability analyses; three factors emerged and internal consistencies (Cronbach's alpha) for subscales and the overall score are reported. The authors tested sex differences via independent-samples t-tests and found no significant differences on the overall ACSS score or on two subscales (Intrapersonal, Social), but women scored significantly higher on the Consider subscale.
section_summary.evidence_source: The 15 items of the Portuguese ACSS were subjected to an exploratory factor analysis (EFA). ... In the present study, Cronbach's ˛ for this overall score was .91. An independent sample t-tests showed that there was no significant sex difference on the overall ACSS score (women M = 3.67, SD = 1.27; men M = 3.61, SD = 1.40), t(309) = 0.36, p = .721, d = 0.04. ... women were significantly more likely to have higher scores on the Consider subscale (women M = 3.93, SD = 1.67; men M = 3.52, SD = 1.86), although the effect size of this difference was small, t(309) = 2.02, p = .045, d = 0.23.
